description: Memory-pipeline behavior imported neutrally as request/stream -> observable outcome. Internal storage shape is NOT imported: old-vs-new payload schema and colForType collection-name mapping are backend-specific (excluded per 01 §7). The rev6 labeled-observation-stream corpus with create|reinforce|supersede|noop ops (14 §1 item 4, [FIXED new in rev6]) is RESOLVED (T14-07): the `memory.router.op.*` cases below are that corpus, scored by `cargo xtask memory-bench` (`crates/xtask/src/memory_bench/`) against `local_rag_memory::router::route`.

cases.title: A supersede target buried past the prompt-candidate cap is still found

provenance.note: Identical observations and expectation to memory.router.op.supersede-existing-en; the only difference is that the target entry is the newest of 56 global entries, so it lands past MAX_PROMPT_CANDIDATES (50). Before D-080 candidate_conflict_set sorted by memory_id ascending and truncated, so the model was shown the 50 oldest fillers and never the entry the window is about. The 55 fillers are deliberately unrelated to the window's wording: their job is to saturate the cap, not to mislead the model.

existing_entries.text: Release notes are written in the imperative mood.
The staging environment is rebuilt every Monday morning.
Container images are tagged with the short commit hash.
Feature flags are removed within two releases of going live.
Database migrations run before the new binary starts.
The design system lives in a separate package.
Screenshots in the docs are captured at 2x scale.
Long-running jobs report progress every thirty seconds.
Error messages name the field that failed validation.
The changelog is generated from merged pull request titles.
Secrets are read from the environment, never from disk.
Timestamps are stored in UTC and rendered in local time.
The onboarding checklist is reviewed each quarter.
Log lines carry a request identifier.
Nightly builds are kept for fourteen days.
Dependency upgrades land in their own commit.
The support rota is published a month ahead.
Draft pull requests do not trigger the full suite.
Fonts are self-hosted rather than fetched from a CDN.
Analytics events use snake_case names.
Backups are verified by restoring them once a month.
The mobile layout is designed before the desktop one.
Retries use exponential backoff with jitter.
Public methods carry doc comments.
The team stand-up is asynchronous on Fridays.
Temporary directories are cleaned up on process exit.
Configuration defaults live next to their documentation.
Incident reviews are blameless and written within a week.
Icons ship as inline SVG.
Cache keys include the schema version.
The linter runs on staged files only.
Panics are reserved for unrecoverable invariants.
Email templates are tested against a plain-text renderer.
Third-party scripts are loaded lazily.
The roadmap is reviewed at the start of each month.
Test fixtures are minimal and hand-written.
Colour contrast is checked against WCAG AA.
Background workers shut down on the first signal.
Documentation examples are compiled as part of the build.
Pagination defaults to twenty items per page.
The search box keeps focus after a query is submitted.
Metrics names are prefixed with the service name.
Uploads larger than ten megabytes are rejected.
The admin panel is reachable only over the internal network.
Translations fall back to English when a key is missing.
Keyboard shortcuts are listed in the help dialog.
Stale branches are deleted after ninety days.
The build fails on any compiler warning.
Sessions expire after two weeks of inactivity.
Empty states explain what to do next.
Rate limits are returned in response headers.
The favicon is regenerated whenever the logo changes.
Audio files are stored outside the repository.
Form submissions are debounced by three hundred milliseconds.
Print stylesheets hide navigation chrome.
Use REST for the internal API.

observations.text: We changed our mind: the internal API will use gRPC instead of REST from now on.
